A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEGA. Their complete text, equations, four tables, ten figures and appendices are readable and matchable, including the new Appendix F in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original human mesh recovery experiments and ablations in Tables 1–3, plus stochastic-generation analyses and unconditional mesh-generation results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports inference timings in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same tokenization, encoder-decoder architecture, losses, masking schedules and deterministic/stochastic generation procedures. The added design discussion does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain AMASS pre-training and unconditional generation, the same four HMR training datasets, and evaluation on 3DPW, EMDB and 3DPW-OCC. The timing measurements introduce no new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in each experiment in Tables 1–3 and Appendix C, including VPoser and NRDF for unconditional generation. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a timing evaluation specifying a GTX 1070 GPU and batch size 1, with comparisons across backbones, inference modes and output counts. Existing accuracy protocols, training schedules, metrics and data splits are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new inference-efficiency analysis examines computational cost across backbones, deterministic/stochastic modes and single versus multiple predictions. Existing masking and pre-training ablations, occlusion tests, error-distribution analyses and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A retains the prediction standard deviations in Table 4 and the discussion of 95% confidence intervals associated with Figure 5. No new run counts, seed information or statistical uncertainty procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Appendix B newly reports deterministic HRNet/ResNet timings of 0.07/0.03 seconds and stochastic ResNet timings of 0.04 seconds for one prediction and 0.23 seconds for 16. Tables 1–4, Appendix C's FID/APD results and the qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and masking/sampling equations are unchanged. The new vertex-versus-SMPL discussion supplies conceptual reasoning, without adding or revising a formal derivation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: masked generative HMR, self-supervised mesh pre-training, flexible deterministic/stochastic inference and claimed state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly explains how tokenization reconstruction error propagates into training targets. Appendix F adds arguments for vertex tokenization and discusses hypothesis scoring as a possible application. Existing extreme-pose limitations and broader-impact qualifications are relocated, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: v4 adds inference hardware, batch-size and timing information, and replaces the promised future code/model release with a project-page pointer. Appendix F also gives a 512 × 8 codebook description inconsistent with the retained embedding dimension L = 9 in Section 3.1; this does not establish a model change.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Sampling Is Matter, MeshPose and NIKI. Section 2.1 more specifically identifies VQ-HPS as the closest related method and expands the architectural distinction, while retaining TokenHMR as related work.

P1.justification: v4 makes focused paragraph revisions and adds explanations, cross-references, acknowledgments and affiliation updates. New Appendix F incorporates the former conclusion's limitations, future work and broader impact. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: All four tables and ten figures are retained. Figures are resized or repositioned, including Figure 4 moving to page 8 and Figures 8–9 sharing space with Appendix F. Some qualitative images have reduced raster resolution; their examples and findings are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix B supplies concrete timing evidence for speed claims that v3 left unquantified, while Section 3.3 and Appendix F clarify design choices and tokenization error. These modest benefits outweigh localized issues in the additions, including the inconsistent codebook dimension and misnumbered ScoreHypo citation. The method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
